pages.en:
“————Hot.”

The discomfort wakes me.

My pajamas hang heavy with sweat, and I have kicked the covers away.

When I wipe my brow, my hand comes away sopping wet, as though I had wrung out a rag.

, So hot.”

I wipe my forehead and feel that it’s wet with sweat.

pages.en:
“————”

…My mind will not work properly.

Has the heat, like some sweltering midsummer night, cooked my brain?

No matter how hard I squeeze my reason, I cannot even tell when I am, or where.

“————”

I go out into the garden.

More than anything, I want to cool this feverish body.

…Is the room hot, or am I?

It is too much trouble to think. I will sleep in the storehouse tonight.

At least it is cold in there.

Whether the night is hot or my body is burning, it will not mat——

“Guh——ah——!”

Sudden pain impales me and drives me to my knees.

“——It… hurts——”

I crouch there for a time, breath coming in ragged gasps.

pages.ja:
……目が覚めた。
熱と痛みの元凶である左腕をぎゅっと掴む。
聖骸布は巻かれたままだ。
がっちりと腕を拘束した赤い布。
動きはするものの、ここまできつく縛られると血の巡りが悪くなる。
それでふと、この布こそが左腕を痛ませているのではないか、と考えた。

pages.en:
…I am awake now.

I clutch my left arm, the source of both heat and pain.

The holy shroud is still wrapped around it.

The red cloth binds the arm tight.

It can move, but tied this firmly, the circulation must be suffering.

And then the thought occurs to me: what if the cloth itself is making the arm hurt?
pages.mirrorMoon:
…I wake up.
I squeeze my left arm, the cause of the heat and the pain.
The Shroud is still wrapped around it.
The red cloth is restraining my arm.
I can move it, but it’s wrapped so tight that the circulation is restricted.
Maybe this cloth is the cause of the pain.

pages.ja:
「案外、布を取れば元通りだったりしてな」
口にした妄想は、ひどく魅力的だった。
そもそも、自分はこの赤い布の中身を見ていない。
あの神父の言葉を信用していない訳じゃないが、あいつにだって間違いはあるだろうし。

pages.en:
“Maybe if I just take this thing off, everything will go back to normal.”

The fantasy is terribly alluring once spoken aloud.

After all, I have never seen what lies beneath the red cloth.

It is not that I distrust the priest, but even he must make mistakes.

Perhaps nothing happened to my real arm at all. Perhaps if I unwind the cloth, I will find the familiar arm I have always known.

My arm cannot truly be made of iron.

The cloth is the only reason it will not move. Once I take it off, surely——
